topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecturer and define the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and the role of environmental exposure versus chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic mutations and microenvironmental factors interact with environmental exposures and random biological chance to influence cancer incidence across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive cancer development, focusing in detail on the etiology and pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic processing to induce direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic tumor promotion mechanisms, developmental windows of vulnerability, and the interplay between cellular initiation and tissue environment.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and evaluating carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and assess carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding remarks summarize the primary themes of the lecture and bring the session to a close.
